what: The authors translate the Python spec of Ethereum's 3-slot-finality (3SF) consensus protocol into TLA+ and use the Apalache model checker to test Accountable Safety: if two conflicting chains are both finalized, at least one third of validators can be shown to have broken a voting rule. They then add hand-made abstractions and re-encode the problem in SMT (CVC5) and Alloy to check larger instances.

what: Introduces A-cast concurrent game structures, a coalition-broadcast restriction of visibility-based CGS that permits private data sharing while retaining decidable ATL model checking. Proves 2-EXPTIME-completeness for A-formulas and models a nested-ATL terrorist-fraud attack on the Hancke–Kuhn distance-bounding protocol. title: A Conference Management System with Verified Document Confidentiality.
what: CoCon is a multiuser,multiconference web application whose deterministic functional kernel is specified in Isabelle and extracted to Scala. Develops bounded-deducibility(BD)security:before a release trigger,each alternative secret sequence permitted by a bound must remain compatible with the observer’s action/output sequence. Mechanizes a sufficient unwinding theorem and ten concrete confidentiality instances. End-to-end web-application confidentiality depends on informal code-generation/wrapper trust arguments. Specifies45authenticated kernel actions and a phase-based conference lifecycle;derives explicit paper/review/discussion/decision/reviewer-identity policies with role/time triggers and permitted version/count information. Gives a four-argument unwinding relation over paired states and remaining secret lists,independent/reaction/exit cases,a decreasing measure,and disjunction-based decomposition. Details a synchronizing PAP2proof and reports two person months including reusable proof infrastructure.
assumptions_limits: Formal target is deterministic input-output kernel behavior and finite traces;observations are selected users’ action/output pairs. No distributed replication,network scheduling,crash recovery,availability/liveness or cryptographic secrecy theorem is presented. Isabelle kernel/logic,code generator,Scala compiler/runtime and external library behavior form trust boundaries. Code generation is used restrictively:terminating deterministic executable specification,no nontrivial data refinement,paper contents mapped to JVM files. Trace isomorphism is argued informally,not formally proved end-to-end. Web wrapper is trusted to invoke only exported step/initial-state operations and display outputs without extra leaks;third-party libraries must resist exploits. Timing channels and lower-level/browser attacks are excluded. Mapping abstract content to mutable JVM files is also an implementation representation boundary,not a theorem in this paper. BD is qualitative possibility-based secrecy. Every compatible alternative is treated as plausible;prior probabilities,externally known behavior patterns and high-user cooperation/Trojan-horse signaling are not generally eliminated. Arbitrary unauthorized coalitions are modeled as a fixed observer group,but authorized-user intentional disclosure is not prevented. Trigger occurrence removes the bound for that trace;it does not establish later confidentiality restoration or revocation. An existential trace witness need not preserve invisible high-level user actions,trace length or all external scheduling knowledge. This flexibility is deliberate and matters when interpreting learn-nothing claims. Confidentiality is relative to chosen value/observation filters,producer functions,trigger and bound. Document histories/identity/count policy must match intended disclosure. The ten independently proved source properties are not a stated theorem of joint secrecy for all combinations of secret sources. Unwinding is a sufficient proof method,not a complete decision procedure. Safety lemmas become automated but high-level unwinding strategies still need interaction;fully automated strategy synthesis/abstraction/model checking are future work.
use_for_goal: A concrete verified service/kernel and relational confidentiality proof relevant to distributed-system specification,refinement trust and evaluating generated proof claims. Offers an expressive policy/witness-construction target beyond invariant checking and illustrates manual strategy versus automated safety obligations. Scala/Isabelle sequential server kernel;no Verus/Rust,TLA+,LLM-agent or replicated consensus case. Its explicit source-to-runtime trust limits are useful when assessing claims of end-to-end verified systems.

title: A Generalised Union of Rely–Guarantee and Separation Logic Using Permission Algebras
what: GenRGSep is an Isabelle/HOL library generalizing rely-guarantee separation logic to resource models without guaranteed units or cancellativity. It supplies permission/multi-unit/single-unit algebra classes,compositional resource constructions,a generic relational-action concurrent language,explicit stabilization operators,and a reported mechanized operational soundness theorem. Identifies why Vafeiadis-style operational safety nearly extends to noncancellative resources but needs stronger preservation of local state on silent framed steps when external choice retains its surrounding command. Conjunction still needs all local resources cancellative. Distinguishes a weaker atomic framing condition from requiring the atomic relation to admit the corresponding unframed transition. Paper’s result concerns the generic logic/library,not a production implementation.
assumptions_limits: Permission algebra requires partial commutativity/associativity,compatibility laws and positivity;it need not have units or cancellation. Multi-unit and single-unit classes add those respective structures. Total HOL addition is only constrained by algebra laws on compatible resources;behavior on incompatible sums cannot silently be used as valid resource composition. Proof system works over local/shared state pairs and relational atomic actions. Environment rely relation constrains shared changes;guarantee constrains observable updates. Local state splits under parallel composition while shared state remains common. Instantiating a real language requires sound resource and atomic-action models beyond this generic framework. Theorem2 says a derivable triple and its precondition imply safe n for every finite n. safe enforces postcondition only when command is skip,checks rely/program/framed steps,and records observable guarantee updates. It does not prove termination,fairness,progress,deadlock freedom or network-fault tolerance. Conjunction rule retains a global side condition:every possible local state must be cancellative. Removing cancellation from the base algebra does not make all standard conjunction reasoning available over arbitrary noncancellative instances. Silent τ transitions must preserve the same unframed local resource in the strengthened frame-safety clause. This is essential to the external-choice proof;allowing merely some decomposed residual resource is insufficient. Observable updates generate guarantee obligations without forcing guarantee reflexivity for silent actions. Predicates are shallow HOL functions;rely/guarantee,stabilization and atomic proof obligations are supplied mathematical relations/predicates. Paper reports an Isabelle mechanization and supplies GitHub/SWH artifact,but does not demonstrate an automated verifier,code extraction or verified compiler connection. The supplied PDF has substantial apparent notation/rule inconsistencies detailed in reader caveats. The record distinguishes the authors’ mechanized-soundness claim from the displayed formulas;no artifact execution checks which formulation is implemented. Displayed rules alone should not be treated as a coherent independently validated formalization.
use_for_goal: Relevant foundation for concurrent systems verification:resource ownership and interference reasoning can compose without assuming cancellative heaps,while individual proof rules retain additional requirements. Useful for evaluating generated proofs/specifications:check algebraic hypotheses,progress versus finite-step safety,stability obligations,and whether displayed rules match kernel-checked artifact. These are reader lessons;paper has no Verus,Rust,TLA+,distributedprotocolorLLMexperiment.

title: A-IC3: Learning-Guided Adaptive Inductive Generalization for Hardware Model Checking
what: A-IC3 adds an online proof-aware contextual multi-armed bandit to IC3 generalization. A PA-LinUCB agent chooses among static and activity-aware CTG/EXCTG strategies from local CTI and global proof-state features, then updates from clause quality and propagation feedback. The method defines an eight-feature context, push-aware reward, seven arms, and globally fixed hyperparameters, then integrates with rIC3 without offline training. Experiments separate safe/unsafe solving, PAR-2, arm-selection phases, and termination-frame counts; case plots show adaptive choices rather than a fixed arm.

title: A Proof-Producing Compiler for Blockchain Applications
what: Augments Cairo0 compiler with per-compilation Lean3 specifications and correctness proofs connecting actual compiled Cairo machine code to user-written high-level functional specifications. Tool harvests compiler metadata and logs; it generates naive function/block specifications and proof scripts, while users prove these imply their desired specifications. Lean checks generated and handwritten proofs. Case verifies secp256k1 arithmetic and public-key recovery for signatures, conditional on model/range assumptions and an admitted elliptic-curve associativity lemma. Does not verify compiler universally or prove total correctness/cryptographic unforgeability. Cairo memory/register values are finite-field elements, memory is immutable,failed assertions have no successor and ill-formed instructions are nondeterministic. ensures quantifies over finite halting traces and promises some reached state satisfying a step-indexed postcondition; recursion/loops use induction on execution length,not a termination proof. Generated specifications use users’ specs of dependencies,allowing modular recursive proofs. Verification symbolically steps assembly via proved small-step instruction lemmas. Compiler flow-tracker identities about allocation-pointer changes are themselves proved in Lean. Range-check pointer intervals are threaded through calls; length mu<=kappa,with public execution length below field characteristic,prevents wraparound. User-facing specs mediate integers,secp field and three-limb Cairo-field representations. Only regular CFGs are supported; tool can fail on arbitrary spaghetti jumps. Generated source-level proofs support interactive debugging and incremental specification reuse without trusting compiler transformations.

quotes.text: All references to the Cairo language in this paper therefore refer to Cairo 0.

If the program counter points to an assert instruction that fails, there is no successor state. If the program counter points to an ill-formed instruction, the value of t is nondeterministic, so verifying that a Cairo program has the intended semantics generally requires establishing that a successful run of the program does not encounter such an instruction.

To handle recursive calls and loops, we do not have to prove termination; the STARK certificate assures a skeptical verifier that the program has terminated, so we need only show that, given that fact, the specification is met.

Our correctness proof needs to use the fact that the total number of range-checked elements does not wrap around the finite field. We achieve this by asserting that µ is, moreover, bounded by the number of steps κ in the execution trace, which is made public in the STARK certification and is always smaller than the characteristic of the field.
Lean allows us to insert a sorry placeholder for the missing proof of associativity; this is the only sorry in our development.
The error, which does not allow the prover to fake a signature but does allow it to claim that a valid signature is invalid, was fixed in the next Cairo release.

title: A Verified and Compositional Translation of LTL to Deterministic Rabin Automata
what: Isabelle/HOL formalization of a modular LTL-to-deterministic-Rabin-automata construction: a logical Master Theorem decomposes formulas into simpler languages, a reusable automata library combines their translations, and executable refinement exports a language-correct StandardML translator with a proved double-exponential state bound. Separates logical decomposition, automata operations and executable data refinement. The transition-system locale separates execute from enabled and represents nondeterministic choices in transition labels. Translation locales explicitly require equivalence refinement, quotient laws and congruence of derivatives/advice. Proves unrestricted-alphabet language equality before finite-alphabet export; identifies unverified text parsing/serialization in the final CLI. Includes a general finite-set induction rule constrained by rank and a derivative/reset construction for GF of least-fixed-point formulas.
assumptions_limits: LTL syntax is in negation normal form with literals, Boolean connectives, X,U,R,W,M; F/G are abbreviations. Semantics concerns infinite words, not finite-trace semantics. μ fragments exclude R/W; ν fragments exclude U/M. The Master Theorem ranges X over least-fixed-point U/M subformulas and Y over greatest-fixed-point R/W subformulas. Advice is not an unchecked oracle: all candidate sets are enumerated and the component languages check the needed GF/FG conditions. Definition22 requires equivp(~), constants-equivalence ≤ ~ ≤ language-equivalence, Abs(Rep x)=x, equality of Abs images iff formula equivalence, and congruence of both af and ν-advice. Language equivalence bounds alone do not suffice to instantiate the locale. Executable instantiation uses propositional equivalence, implemented with prior Boolean-expression-checker code. Theorem25 covers abstract DRA over UNIV; executable Theorem27 covers Pow(atoms φ), finite because the input syntax has finitely many atoms. This finite-alphabet restriction enables explicit DFS exploration. It is not a direct statement that the exported automaton accepts words with arbitrary extraneous propositions without a projection convention. Lemma26 is a verified upper bound on reachable state count, not an empirical speed claim or a new lower-bound proof. The abstract claims asymptotic optimality against a known lower bound. Concrete alphabet enumeration/output can still be enormous. Core correctness is relative to Isabelle/HOL definitions and trusted proof/code-generation infrastructure. Final LTL parser and HOA serializer are explicitly unverified; compilation uses mlton or polyc. This paper does not establish end-to-end correctness from a user text string through machine execution and serialized output. Automata acceptance is introduced at concrete levels; union/intersection are not all proved once in the most general transition-system locale. Executable refinements similarly live mainly at concrete representations. Figure1 is a selected operation inventory, not a complete Boolean algebra or complement implementation for every automaton. Only A2/GF(μLTL) is detailed in the proceedings construction section; A1 and A3 are said to be formalized analogously and their proof exposition is deferred. General framework potential for NBA/LDBA or generalized/transition-based DRA does not mean those derived translators are completed here; §6 lists extensions as future work. No benchmark suite, runtime/state-count experiments, machine specification, repeats or quantitative comparison with Spot/other translators. Evidence is mathematical/formal development and an illustrative command; reader did not run the translator, Isabelle session or downstream tools.

title: A Verified Compositional Algorithm for AI Planning
what: HOL4 soundness proof for synthesizing a concrete plan by composing instantiated solutions to an augmented descriptive quotient. Builds a polymorphic factored transition-system library, sufficient subplan precedence/coverage conditions and an action-filtering repair. Formalization exposes two missing assumptions in an earlier mathematical algorithm and generalizes soundness beyond Boolean finite-state symmetry-derived quotients. Needed initial assignments, a pairwise precedence relation, coverage by actual subproblems, bijective variable renaming, cross-instantiation variable consistency and restoration of shared needed resources jointly justify concatenation. A total no-op semantics for inapplicable actions makes individually harmless plan steps dangerous after composition; rem-cless deletes them before instantiation/concatenation. The final theorem is conditional on supplied quotient, valid instantiations and a quotient solution, not a verified general-purpose planner search procedure.
assumptions_limits: States are finite maps from variable type α to arbitrary value type β. Actions are pairs of finite maps for preconditions/effects; applying one with unsatisfied preconditions leaves the state unchanged. Effects override existing assignments. This differs from classical planning semantics that prohibit inapplicable steps. Valid problems require the initial-state domain equal the union of action domains and the goal domain contained there. Although β and the action set can be infinite/uncountable, each valid state is a finite map and a returned plan is a finite action list. Generic assignment semantics does not already formalize arbitrary continuous dynamics or functional numeric preconditions/effects. A solution consists of actions from the problem’s action set and reaches a state extending the goal. Theorems establish soundness when the premises hold; they do not promise finding a quotient, a plan, complete reachability search, optimality, termination of a subplanner, or successful planning for every solvable concrete input. Needed assignments include initial assignments occurring in any action precondition or the goal. They are conservative sufficient support, not a claimed smallest plan-dependent set. Transfer of a plan to another compatible state also requires every step’s precondition hold when run from the needed partial state. Precedence requires the first goal contain the second problem’s shared needed assignments and both goals have identical assignments on the intersection of the two problem domains. Concatenation requires this relation for every earlier/later pair, not merely adjacent problems. Subproblem coverage requires consistent initial submaps, action-set inclusion and covering every concrete goal assignment. Variable instantiations must be bijective on relevant variable sets, and pwise-valid prevents distinct quotient variables from colliding across different instantiations. Shared quotient variables may map to the same concrete variable. Final HOL statement additionally requires distinct instantiation functions and injectivity of the induced instantiated-problem mapping. The quotient goal is augmented to restore initial values of common needed variables; the final theorem requires the augmented instantiated problems cover the concrete problem. Any ordering of a finite valid instantiation list then works after rem-cless filtering. No assumption that the quotient came from symmetry is needed once these explicit conditions hold. The assurance is HOL4 theorem derivation over the specified action semantics/library. The paper does not give an extracted implementation refinement, end-to-end parser/executable proof, verified symmetry detector or verified subplanner. Reader did not rerun the available scripts. No distributed-system implementation, Verus/Rust proof, TLA+ integration, LLM agent experiment or user study is evaluated. Murphi compositional model checking is a suggested adaptation, not a verified result of this development.
use_for_goal: A concrete proof-engineering example for agents: a semantically valid subplan can fail under composition because a hidden environmental assumption changes. Explicit support/precedence/coverage and removal of inactive steps are transferable specification lessons. Reader inference: analogous resource restoration obligations arise in distributed protocol composition, and theorem search/repeated hypotheses are automation targets. No direct distributed/TLA+/Verus or LLM evaluation is supplied.

title: A Verified Cost Model for Call-By-Push-Value
what: Defines time and peak-term-size semantics for a closed untyped core of call-by-push-value extended with pseq, and reports HOL4 proofs of constant-factor simulations by substitution/heap machines plus a weak-call-by-value translation. Handwritten Turing-machine simulations interleave substitution and heap evaluation to claim polynomial time and constant-factor space reasonableness, relying on prior WCBV results in the reverse direction. Distinguishes formalized intermediate results from unformalized interleaving; printed formulas and transition rules have concrete issues detailed below. Records exact syntax/reduction costs and unary index-sensitive size, machine compilation formats and bounds, size-versus-pointer explosion, compressed heap output, binary iteration/space argument, necessity conjecture for pseq, mechanization boundary and artifact pointer. Gives concrete reader checks of displayed size inequality, heap environment links and return-value correspondence without attributing these printed defects to unchecked HOL4 scripts.
assumptions_limits: §§1–3, pp.2–5: reasonable means mutual polynomial-time/constant-space-factor simulation with Turing machines, above linear input-resource regimes; sublinear classes such as LOGSPACE excluded. Core calculus untyped and closed at top level, two mutually recursive syntactic categories: values var/thunk; computations lambda,app,force,ret,seq,pseq,let. General products/effects absent. Typed terms are a subset, but no theorem about an actual production-language cost model supplied. §3, pp.4–6: pseq m2 m1 n evaluates m1 then m2 and substitutes their values at indices0and1 in n. It binds two results without extra nested seq depth. Time charges lambda/ret0, application/seq/pseq/let1 plus premise costs, force(thunk m)2 plus subcomputation. Thus time is this defined weighted semantics, not simply number of all source syntactic nodes traversed or machine instructions. Big-step semantics only gives finite costs for terminating evaluations. §3, pp.5–6: term size counts each constructor1and variable indexxas1+x. Space is maximum intermediate syntax size with unevaluated context/results included in max formulas. Indices effectively cost unary space, not constant-size identifiers. Translation-induced index shifts can therefore cause quadratic growth even when constructor count grows linearly. Same unannotated evaluation underlies time and space judgments. §4, pp.6–7: substitution compiler gamma serializes syntax with delimiter tokens; heap gamma-prime differs by ret v→gamma-prime(v)++retT. Program size1+sum token sizes, with varT x costing1+x. Delimiter extraction scans nested marker pairs and is undefined on malformed unmatched input. Compiler/machine invariants must guarantee well-formed programs; extraction is not a unit-time Turing operation. §5.2, pp.8–9: substitution machine task/value stacks perform closed substitutions eagerly, discard empty task fragments and retain suspended values/computations in value stack. These are abstract transition counts; one transition may copy or scan a large program. §5.3, pp.9–10: heap machine uses closures(program,environment-pointer), append-only heap cells(closure,previous-pointer), lookup traverses environment chain. Printed pseq environment link and final ret correspondence need repair below. §§2/6.1, pp.3–4/11–14: substitution evaluation has exponential-time copying when source steps cause size explosion; heap sharing avoids that but pointer representation can exceed source-space factor. This absorbs binary step-counter space in O(S). It must be restricted to terminating reductions; divergent deterministic terms can revisit a state. The printed counting proof uses a five-symbol recurrence inconsistent with the listed token alphabet, although a larger constant alphabet can still support an exponential-count argument. §6.2 Theorem22, pp.15–16: WCBV terms var/app/lambda with weak evaluation translate c(lambda t)=ret(thunk(lambda c(t))); application uses pseq c(u)c(t)(app(forcevar0)var1). title: A Verified Decision Procedure for Univariate Real Arithmetic with the BKR Algorithm
what: Isabelle/HOL correctness proof of a BKR-style univariate real-arithmetic decision procedure with rational-coefficient polynomial atoms. Computes exact realizable sign assignments by recursive matrix combination and reduction using Tarski queries, then decides existential/universal closure of Boolean polynomial formulas. Supplies executable SML and supporting matrix/rank theorems, with ten illustrative microbenchmarks. Connects formula semantics to complete sign determination, reduces unrestricted sign regions to roots of coprime polynomials using squarefree factorization/Rolle/root bounds, and proves the matrix equation separately from invertibility. Kronecker combination preserves invertibility but temporarily includes impossible sign patterns; zero-count column removal and rank-preserving pivot-row selection restore an invertible reduced system. Proves cached matrix consistency and coverage invariants, and exposes coefficient growth as the practical bottleneck despite fewer queries.
assumptions_limits: Formal input grammar has atoms p>0,p≥0,p=0 with rational-coefficient univariate p, combined by conjunction/disjunction. The proved top-level operations decide ∀x phi or ∃x phi over one real variable. Negation/disequality can be normalized using signed polynomials, but arbitrary multivariate quantifier alternation and full real QE are not delivered here. Restricted sign theorem requires p!=0 and each q coprime to p, ruling out zero signs for q at p roots. Preliminary squarefree/pairwise-coprime factorization and separate zero-root cases are needed to cover unrestricted input atoms, including signs0. A Renegar variant avoiding coprimality was formalized after acceptance but its full details are omitted. M*w=v needs distinct candidate sign vectors covering every realizable assignment and valid subset indices. The theorem alone does not imply square/invertible M; separate inductive invariants establish it. Roots and actual count-vector definitions are semantic/nonconstructive specifications, not procedures for explicitly isolating real algebraic roots. The algorithm maintains distinct sign vectors of correct length, all realizable signs included, a cached matrix equal to the matrix computed from subset/sign lists, and matrix invertibility. Only reduction guarantees exact signs; base/combination may overapproximate. Column deletion retains full column rank, then selected rows form a square full-rank matrix. The empty polynomial-list restricted case is handled separately: no roots of p gives no consistent assignment; otherwise the result is the singleton empty vector. The sampling construction using derivative of the product is presented for nontrivial factors; constant/degenerate preprocessing cases should not be inferred from that displayed formula alone. Optimized univariate BKR has potential for parallel polylogarithmic time, but this development is unoptimized/sequential and does not formalize that complexity theorem. Both parallelization and a compatible formal complexity framework remain future work. The cited Tarski-query arithmetic-operation estimate excludes coefficient bit growth. Export to SML compiled by MLton supplies experimental executables, not automatically a kernel-checked Isabelle proof result for each native run. Making BKR practical as an Isabelle tactic is future work. By contrast the measured univ_rcf comparator explicitly checks untrusted Mathematica certificates by reflection inside Isabelle. Bivariate/multivariate AppendixA is informal motivation, not a verified multivariate algorithm. The original multivariate BKR complexity analysis has a known error; the paper proposes future variants and does not claim to repair/formalize all multivariate complexity bounds. Performance evidence is ten microbenchmarks on one laptop, one-hour cutoff, three-decimal reported seconds. No repetitions/variance or broader representative suite is given. Naive matrix-equation implementation is unverified, and the external-solver tactic includes startup overhead. No LLM-agent, distributed-protocol, Rust/Verus or TLA+ result is measured.
use_for_goal: Reader inference: illustrates semantic proof obligations for automated arithmetic used inside systems proofs and proof-writing agents: completeness of candidate signs, justified pruning, type/domain premises, and executable-to-prover trust boundaries. title: A Verified Earley Parser
what: Isabelle/HOL formalization of an inductive Earley recognizer, refinement through a bin-wise fixed-point algorithm to executable functional lists, and a pointer-guided parser producing one parse tree. Recognizer correctness and successful parse-tree existence equivalence require terminal-only input and an epsilon-free grammar. Returned-tree soundness and a termination argument are proved for generated pointer structures. Explains why one-pass list-bin processing misses completion opportunities for epsilon rules and retains an explicit epsilon-free premise. Separates item equality, refinement, pointer invariants, single-tree soundness and tree-existence equivalence from enumeration of all parses. Uses first reduction-pointer monotonicity to terminate even for cyclic grammars; gives informal O(n^4) time and O(n^3) pointer-space estimates, rather than attributing optimal Earley bounds to this implementation.
assumptions_limits: Grammar is a finite rule list plus start symbol over a common symbol type. Nonterminals are all rule LHS symbols plus the start symbol; terminals are the remaining symbols. is_word G omega excludes nonterminals from the input. Abstract item completeness and correctness explicitly assume is_word. The inductive Earley specification supports epsilon rules, but executable Earley_eq_Earley_L, correctness_recognizer and correctness_build_tree_Earley_L require epsilon_free G: every RHS is nonempty. Lifting this restriction is future work. No verified epsilon-elimination preprocessing is delivered here. Each bin contains distinct items with end index equal to bin index. List insertion appends new items and merges reduction pointers into existing entries. Termination of bin processing relies on well-formed bounded items and finite candidate counts, not arbitrary malformed bin arguments. build_tree_prime termination requires wf_tree_input: sound_ptrs, mono_red_ptr, valid bin/input indices and valid entry index. Pointer soundness includes earlier origin bins for reductions, bounds and operation semantics. Only the FIRST reduction triple is required to have a strictly earlier reduction entry within the current bin. wf_item_yield_build_tree_prime additionally assumes wf_bins. Returned-tree corollary assumes epsilon_free and successful build_tree over Earley_L-generated bins, and proves rule-tree well-formedness, start root and full input yield. Existential successful tree iff derivation additionally assumes is_word. The algorithm extracts one parse tree, not a forest enumerating every ambiguous or cyclic derivation. Nevertheless the final theorem DOES establish existence of a returned tree iff a valid derivation exists under its premises. The phrase no completeness for trees concerns all possible trees, not failure to recognize some valid word. Partial functions in HOL use domain-theoretic definitions; termination is proved on stated valid inputs. Option None representing undefinedness is not a runtime detector that can return after discovering an infinite computation. Arbitrary externally supplied pointer cycles are outside the proved termination domain. Complexity is explicitly informal with fixed grammar: rule count and maximum RHS size are constants. More than 6,000 formalization lines are reported, but no formal complexity theorem or proof-effort breakdown is supplied. Scala extraction and execution do not constitute a verified compiler/runtime chain. Evaluation measures the exported recognizer, not a full byte-level lexer or full parse-tree production pipeline. Five toy grammars, unary inputs a^n and ten-run means do not establish representative production workload performance. Hardware, Scala/JVM versions, exact source dataset, variance and raw timings are not supplied in §7. Imperative cached refinement, grammar indexing, next-symbol grouping and epsilon support remain future work. No Verus, Rust, TLA+, distributed-system implementation or LLM agent is evaluated.
use_for_goal: Reader inference: a case study for specification/refinement audits in trusted parsing of generated proofs or distributed-system input. It demonstrates how a general inductive specification can have a narrower proved implementation, why pointer invariants and scheduling restrictions matter, and why proof correctness, completeness of one answer, completeness of every answer and runtime cost need separate evidence. It supplies no direct distributed-protocol, Verus/verified-Rust, TLA+ or LLM-agent evaluation.

title: A Verified LL(1) Parser Generator
what: Vermillion is a Coq-verified LL(1) parse table generator and a table-parameterized parser with user-defined semantic actions. The generator has soundness and conditional completeness proofs. The parser has soundness and completeness relative to an LL(1) prefix derivation relation, terminates even with malformed tables, and avoids internal left-recursion errors with correct tables. Separates generic termination from error exclusion under table correctness; details a finite-set complement measure for dataflow analysis and a lexicographic accessibility proof for mutually recursive parsing. A dependent suffix result moves token-length reasoning into erased proofs, removing an observed extraction performance problem. Generator completeness has an explicit duplicate-production restriction, and parser correctness includes the semantic value and unparsed suffix.
assumptions_limits: Grammar gives a start nonterminal, finite production sequence and Coq semantic type for each symbol. Tokens pair terminals with values; each production carries a dependently typed Coq semantic action from its RHS tuple to its LHS type. These are total Coq functions, not unrestricted effectful host-language callbacks. Correctness is relative to sym_derives_prefix, whose DerNT rule includes LOOKAHEAD. The paper does not separately prove equivalence to an unrestricted context-free derivation relation. Definitions of NULLABLE, FIRST, FOLLOW and lookahead are part of the specification to assess. parseTableOf_sound requires successful generation and establishes parse_table_correct. parseTableOf_complete additionally requires unique_productions: duplicates are compared ignoring actions. It yields a returned map extensionally equal to the given correct map, not definitional identity of finite-map representations. parse_sound, parse_complete and parse_terminates_without_error assume parse_table_correct tbl g. Total termination also covers arbitrary tables, where dynamic cycle detection may return Error. Invalid token input may return Reject even with a correct table; absence of Error does not mean every input is accepted. Parser and derivation both describe prefixes and remainders. The top-level parse wrapper does not test that the returned remainder is empty. Full-input acceptance requires the caller to enforce that condition. No byte-level lexer correctness theorem is given. Left recursion in §4.3 is lookahead-qualified nullable_path g la s s, not every syntactic occurrence reachable on a left edge. Nullable prefixes permit reaching the next nonterminal without consumption. This definition matters for unproductive grammar cycles with no lookahead facts. Termination of the Coq functions is established without fuel. This excludes infinite parser recursion in the formal setting; it does not establish quantitative resource bounds, extracted stack safety, or immunity to every resource-exhaustion attack. OCaml extraction, OCaml compiler/runtime, finite-map implementation execution and the external lexer/tokenizer remain execution trust considerations. The paper reports extraction and testing, not a verified compiler chain from Coq to machine code. JSON evaluation is one small dataset with means of ten trials; hardware, exact dataset, tool versions and dispersion are not specified in §5. The lexer omits Unicode escape sequences. Menhir uses LR(1), Vermillion LL(1), so the measured ratio does not isolate verification overhead. The paper describes observed linear behavior and theoretical LL(1) complexity, but does not supply a formal complexity theorem for the complete extracted implementation. Removing unreachable dynamic errors and emitting specialized parser source code are future work.
use_for_goal: Reader inference: relevant to trustworthy parsers for agent-generated specifications, proof certificates and distributed-system inputs. The useful pattern is to state exact input semantics, separate termination from success, keep generator completeness premises explicit, and track extraction/lexing trust. The dependent-proof optimization also illustrates why executable performance must be checked after proof-oriented implementation. The paper does not evaluate distributed protocols, Verus, verified Rust, TLA+ or LLM agents.

what: Parametric Markov chains occur quite naturally in various applications: they can be used for a conservative analysis of probabilistic systems (no matter how the parameter is chosen, the system works to specification); they can be used to find optimal settings for a parameter; they can be used to visualise the influence of system parameters; and they can be used to make it easy to adjust the analysis for the case that parameters change. title: Formal Verification of Blockchain Nonforking in DAG-Based BFT Consensus with Dynamic Stake
what: Formalizes a DAG-based BFT consensus protocol whose validator set and stake can change at every block, and machine-checks blockchain nonforking in ACL2 under a less-than-one-third faulty-stake condition for every active committee. The labeled transition system models validators, certificates, DAGs, network messages, rounds, dynamic bonding/unbonding, lookback active committees, anchor elections/commitments and block generation. Bonding changes become active only after a fixed lookback, resolving the DAG/blockchain circular dependency. The proof establishes interdependent invariants for committee agreement, certificate and DAG nonequivocation, previous quorums, anchor presence/voters/paths/nonforking, and blockchain nonforking. Anchor nonforking uses voter/quorum stake intersection; certificate nonequivocation uses signer quorum intersection, and both are proved together because each depends on the other through committee agreement. The ACL2 development has about 20,000 lines and verifies in under one minute on an Apple M3 Max (under two minutes single-core), applying to arbitrarily long executions and arbitrarily large states. The model intentionally includes deadlocking and other executions beyond an implementation, so safety transfers to implementations as subsets but liveness is not established.

assumptions_limits: Correct validators follow the abstract protocol and faulty validators are Byzantine; each active committee must have faulty stake at most fstk(w)<nstk(w)/3, with quorum stake qstk=nstk−fstk. Signatures/addresses are idealized and cryptographic details are omitted. The model is nondeterministic and a superset of implementation executions; validators can advance without certificates and deadlock, and the authors explicitly note that proving liveness would require augmenting the model. Only blockchain nonforking and related invariants are proved; performance, synchronization, transaction validity, fairness and implementation behavior are not evaluated. The ACL2 state-transition system and nonforking predicate are trusted modeling boundaries.
use_for_goal: A directly relevant machine-checked proof pattern for dynamic distributed consensus: model protocol transitions, stake-weighted quorums and committee changes, then prove interdependent invariants by induction. The explicit trusted-model boundary and deadlocking superset are valuable cautions when transferring ACL2/TLA+/Verus safety proofs to implementations or claiming liveness.

title: Automated and Scalable Verification of Integer Multipliers.
what: Gives an ACL2-verified rewrite procedure for functional correctness of concrete signed/unsigned multiplier circuits. It proves symbolic SVL execution equals ACL2 integer multiplication with specified extensions and bit truncation. title: Adam: Causality-Based Synthesis of Distributed Systems
what: Presents the Adam Java implementation of symbolic Petri-game synthesis: a separate controller for each process uses its causal past and exchanges knowledge at joint transitions. A winning strategy avoids bad places and avoids introducing deadlocks. The paper sketches a finite two-player reduction and reports controller-synthesis benchmarks. Cuts are maximal concurrent sets of places annotated by enabled decision sets and type-1/type-2 system tokens. Type-2 tokens will never synchronize, even indirectly, with the environment; type-1 tokens are blocked until its next move. Environment choices are delayed until an mcut so independent system choices cannot depend on unseen environment choices. The BDD encoding assigns places to tokens rather than arbitrary subsets of places. Phase 1 computes valid type-2 cuts by greatest fixed point; phase 2 combines greatest/least fixed points for winning mcuts and their predecessors; phase 3 extracts a strategy and per-player projections. Net invariants compact the place encoding.

title: Faster Statistical Model Checking for Unbounded Temporal Properties
what: Introduces SimAdaptive, a black-box statistical model-checking algorithm that monitors simulation prefixes to infer bottom strongly connected components (BSCCs), stopping runs early while retaining confidence guarantees for unbounded reachability, full LTL and mean-payoff properties. A path's candidate BSCC is defined by a suffix that is a graph BSCC; k-candidates and strong candidates bound false detection using the minimum positive transition probability pmin. Candidate lifetimes and a union bound yield Algorithm ReachedBSCC with error δ, which feeds sequential probability-ratio testing for reachability. The paper extends the construction to LTL and derives mean-payoff estimators with bounded expected error, then proves an expected runtime bound depending on transient depth R, BSCC size B and hitting time T. Prism experiments compare SimAdaptive against topology-agnostic simulation, topology-aware analysis and numerical model checking across huge benchmark chains.

title: Formula size game and model checking for modal substitution calculus

title: AI4SLT: Empirical Processes in Lean 4 for Formal Statistical Learning Theory
what: Reports a Lean4 library for empirical-process learning theory: Gaussian functional inequalities/concentration, covering and chaining culminating in Dudley’s entropy integral, localized least-squares error bounds, linear regression and ℓ1-image covering. Authors report about30,000lines, over1000theorems/lemmas, about500supervised hours with Claude Code/Opus4.5, and compilation without sorry/custom axioms. Provides a detailed human–AI proof-engineering case study; it does not experimentally establish autonomous research or a causal speedup. Builds coordinate-resampling invariance for heterogeneous independent distributions; Efron–Stein, Rademacher/CLT Gaussian Poincaré, entropy duality/subadditivity, Bernoulli-to-Gaussian log-Sobolev and Herbst concentration. Explicit C1/Sobolev density and mollification handle analytic extension. Dudley uses recursive projections with step distance εk rather than3εk/2, finite-net bounds, a nonnegative shift for Fatou, and separability/path continuity. Covering numbers use WithTop Nat; entropy/integrals have ENNReal canonical versions and real wrappers. Least-squares master theorem exposes sphere nonemptiness, supremum integrability/boundedness and critical-radius hypotheses; ℓ1 covering uses Maurey’s probabilistic finite-net construction. Four preserved task specifications show the entropy-convergence proof evolving from a vague Fatou instruction to a shifted ENNReal proof with explicit API dependencies.
assumptions_limits: Artifact correctness/build size and no-sorry/no-custom-axiom status are author reports, not independently reproduced. Ordinary Lean/Mathlib foundations and the compiler/kernel remain trusted. The phrase without axiom is clarified by task rules as no custom axioms, not an axiom-free foundational logic. Reported Gaussian concentration is for finite positive dimension, positive Lipschitz constant and threshold under standard product Gaussian measure. Dudley requires σ,D>0, a nonempty totally bounded index set, a pathwise-zero anchor, measurable coordinates, integrable exponential increments, finite entropy integral and continuous sample paths; not arbitrary stochastic processes. Displayed Sobolev density/LSI theorems require differentiability and continuous derivatives plus square-integrability; the LSI listing additionally assumes integrability of g²log(g²). They do not formalize every weak-derivative W1,2 function from the bare MemW12Gaussian predicate. The master error theorem assumes f*∈F, star-shaped shifted class, any positive radius satisfying the critical inequality, an ERM for every noise vector, a nonempty sphere at sqrt(tδ), integrable localized absolute suprema at two radii and boundedness. The displayed theorem does not require δ to be the smallest solution. It bounds fixed-design empirical prediction error, not arbitrary population excess risk. Local Gaussian-complexity capacity control additionally assumes total boundedness of the empirical image, finite entropy integral, path continuity and positive/negative supremum integrability. These are proof premises, not a demonstration that every new function class satisfies them. The linear rate theorem has constants C1,C2 existentially quantified after n,model/design and estimator; the printed signature permits these constants to depend on those inputs. It therefore does not by itself express uniform numerical constants or a minimax lower bound. Rank>0 and n>0 are explicit; main prose n≥d is not a displayed signature premise. ℓ1-constrained regression is presented via a normalized-design covering theorem and an asserted rate; no complete final ℓ1 statistical-rate Lean signature or explicit tuning-dependent Lasso equivalence is supplied. Sparse support recovery/restricted-eigenvalue fast rates are not established here. Workflow percentages and failure reduction are approximate retrospective project observations. No controlled comparison, complete attempt counts, randomized assignment, uncertainty intervals, token/cost accounting or human-only timing baseline is supplied. Declaration shares do not measure shares of human/AI effort. First/comprehensive/all-infrastructure novelty claims are author judgments. The paper does not establish exhaustive coverage of statistical learning theory, distributed protocols, Verus, verified Rust or TLA+.
use_for_goal: Directly relevant to agents constructing specifications/proofs: gives concrete human specification structure, mathematical counterexample review, failed-target diagnosis, modular lemma construction and cleanup. title: AKR: A Model Checker for an Adaptative Probabilistic Knowing-How Logic
what: Presents AKR, an open-source Python checker for adaptive probabilistic knowing-how logic. It parses PRISM probabilistic LTS models, regular-expression perceptions, and Khq properties; builds live DFAs, synchronizes products, and delegates minimum reachability probabilities to PRISM. The paper states the polynomial recursive checking algorithm: Boolean cases recurse over states, while Khq builds a product for each perception DFA with a fresh source state and checks minimum probability of reaching DFA-final goal states. It explains NFA determinization and live-DFA conversion, AST parsing with Lark, a distinct synchronization from PRISM, strategy extraction, and output statistics. The hotel-cleaning example makes adaptation concrete: action outcomes change room-cleaning counts and plans may switch based on outcomes. Experiments vary room counts 4–100 and three regular-expression perceptions, isolating star-operator and expression-length effects.

title: MDPs as Distribution Transformers: Affine Invariant Synthesis for Safety Objectives.
short_name: Akshay et al. affine MDP invariants
what: Treats MDPs as transformers of probability distributions and synthesizes affine inductive distributional invariants together with strategies proving distribution-based safety. AlgMemLess targets memoryless strategies with relative completeness; AlgDist handles distribution-dependent general strategies with sound but incomplete Handelman-based constraints. The paper proves that distribution strategies depending only on the current distribution suffice, and that an inductive distributional invariant contained in the safe set is a sound and complete certificate. AlgMemLess templates action probabilities and a conjunction of affine inequalities, uses Farkas' lemma to eliminate universal quantifiers, and has soundness, relative completeness, and PSPACE bounds. AlgDist uses quotients of affine expressions for action probabilities; positivity constraints remove denominators, and Handelman's theorem produces a sound bounded-product translation, losing completeness. The framework handles initialized and uninitialized cases, restricted initial constraints, and can extend to polynomial invariants via Putinar's Positivstellensatz. A prototype in Python/SymPy/PySMT with Z3 and MathSAT solved Running, Chain, Split, PageRank, and Insulin-131 I examples.

assumptions_limits: Safety sets are finite conjunctions of affine inequalities over finite-state MDP distributions; initialized safety is Positivity-hard even for Markov chains. AlgMemLess is complete only relative to affine invariants and memoryless strategies; AlgDist's Handelman translation is incomplete, parameterized by product bound K, and assumes compact antecedent sets for the theorem motivation. Existential nonlinear real arithmetic is decidable but solver performance varies by orders of magnitude and can take hours. Experiments are unoptimized and small; no claim of scalability or complete decision procedure for general distribution safety is made.
use_for_goal: Formal-methods evidence for invariant-based safety certificates and automated strategy synthesis under hard probabilistic dynamics. The sound/completeness distinctions and solver sensitivity are relevant when evaluating automated agents that produce specifications or proofs.

title: ALGO: Synthesizing Algorithmic Programs with LLM-Generated Oracle Verifiers
what: ALGO separates an LLM coder from an LLM-generated reference verifier. The verifier is prompted to produce a semantically correct but inefficient exhaustive oracle; random constrained inputs compare candidate outputs against oracle outputs and return failures for iterative refinement. It supports implicit,instruction-enumerating and iterative searchers and is model-agnostic at the framework level. On CodeContests and recent LeetCode tasks the authors report improved n@k/pass rates over Codex,CodeT,PG-TD and ChatGPT Code Interpreter. The method is statistical testing/reranking: passing generated inputs is not a formal proof, and the oracle itself is only empirically checked. Formalizes algorithm synthesis as (Q,J), with J=JT∧JS separating efficiency and semantic correctness; oracle PO need satisfy JS only. An input generator samples bounded random inputs (maximum each input variable length10); candidate and oracle outputs are compared. Search strategy is π(P|Q)=ΣI π(P|I)π(I|Q), with examples implicit model sampling,enumerated algorithm ideas such as Binary Search/Sorting,and token-level iterative pruning. ChatGPT Code Interpreter generates verifier oracle and input generator at temperature1,rerolling until examples pass; TLE/RE oracle outputs are manually judged where possible. Codex/CodeT use1000 candidates and ChatGPT/PG-TD use20; n@k is fraction of problems solved by any top-n among k after reranking. CodeContests has165 test problems; LeetCode has35 new problems released concurrently/after GPT-4 to reduce contamination. Table2 reports A LGO w/Codex5.60 versus Codex0.70 and CodeT2.10 at1@1000; A LGO w/PG-TD1.57 versus0.67 at1@20; A LGO w/ChatGPT12.00 versus4.40 at1@20. Oracle semantic correctness is88.5% LeetCode and72% CodeContests; generated-test agreement with the system judge is94.78% vs57.39% examples on CodeContests and74.29% vs68.57% on LeetCode,with coverage89.39% vs85.78% and93.00% vs90.32%. Same-coder Table4 gives ALGO tests12.0% at1@20 vs examples4.4% and ChatGPT tests6.8%. More than30 generated tests yields little extra gain. The car-repair case shows exhaustive oracle O(2^m),wrong greedy candidate rejected on one generated input and correct O(n log m) binary search accepted,matching online judge verdicts.

assumptions_limits: Oracle correctness is only tested empirically. Random finite tests can miss semantic bugs; generated oracle errors directly contaminate verifier verdicts. The paper reports88.5% LeetCode and72% CodeContests semantic oracle correctness,not100% or a formal guarantee. Reference-oracle generation assumes exhaustive search is feasible for bounded generated inputs and that an LLM can implement it from a clear prompt. Input values are constrained by maximum length10 and cases timing out/recursing in the oracle are skipped,which can bias verification coverage. Generated oracle may be inefficient; candidate efficiency is separately judged by the online system judge. Agreement on samples does not establish full-judge correctness or asymptotic complexity. Codex candidate set is reused from CodeT because Codex was unavailable; ChatGPT Code Interpreter is an old GPT-3.5/text-davinci-002-code release. Baseline implementations and budgets follow prior settings but are not modern models. CodeContests comparison uses all165 test problems; LeetCode uses35 manually category-annotated recent problems. n@k and pass rates depend on random sampling,rules and reranking; no confidence intervals are reported for Tables2–4. Verification compares execution outputs and can return failed cases; there is no formal specification extraction,proof certificate,adversarial input guarantee or machine-checked proof. The supplied GitHub artifact and source were not rerun. LeetCode algorithm-category enumeration is assisted:the manually annotated instruction set for each problem is guaranteed to include a correct algorithm category (§4.2). It does not address Verus/Rust,TLA+,distributed protocols or formal proof generation beyond ordinary code synthesis; relevance is methodological.

title: Algorithms for Model Checking HyperLTL and HyperCTL*
what: Gives a direct alternating-Büchi-automaton construction for finite-state HyperLTL/HyperCTL* model checking, including quantifier alternation via nondeterminization and complementation. For a restricted alternation-free fragment, reduces checking to a small symbolic circuit with bad-state and strong-fairness constraints. Uses ABC to analyze hardware information flow, cross-execution symmetry of a finite Bakery implementation, and error-code Hamming distance. Preserves the temporal-placement restrictions in alternation-free syntax, current-path branching semantics, formula versus explicit-state complexity, latch-count encoding bound and assumptions behind circuit simplifications. Documents concrete invalid-ID, scheduling/tie-breaking and reset-polarity counterexamples, all benchmark rows, intended information flows versus vulnerabilities and missing quantitative-flow/experimental details.
assumptions_limits: §2: Kripke structures have a successor from every state, hence infinite paths. Path assignments advance synchronously; a newly quantified path starts at the current state of the most recently quantified path epsilon. HyperLTL places all quantifiers in a prefix; HyperCTL* permits branching quantification inside temporal operators. These are finite-state model results, not parameterized proofs over arbitrary process counts. §3.1 Definition2: alternation-free means one quantifier type in negation normal form plus placement restrictions: no existential in the left of Until or right of Release; no universal in the right of Until or left of Release. Boolean combinations of separately checked blocks are handled. A formula with no textual ∀/∃ switch can still incur extra alternation through a forbidden temporal placement. §3.1: standard Boolean/Next/Until/Release automata are combined bottom up. Existential path elimination first applies Miyano–Hayashi nondeterminization, then products with the Kripke structure and projects a state component. This preserves a common witness path across alternating branches; projecting arbitrary alternating branches independently is not the construction. §3.1 Theorem2 states PSPACE-completeness in formula size and NLOGSPACE-completeness in explicit Kripke-structure size. This is not a logarithmic-space or polynomial-time claim in the number of circuit latches: a circuit represents an exponentially large state graph. Proposition1 gives correctness with structural-induction explanation; no mechanized metatheory or verified implementation is supplied. §3.2: full logic uses complementation of alternating automata and nondeterminization. With g(0,n)=n and g(k,n)=c^g(k-1,n), Theorem4 gives NSPACE(g(k,|formula|)) and NSPACE(g(k-1,|K|)), defining level-1 as NLOGSPACE. These are upper bounds parameterized by alternation depth; the practical circuit implementation/evaluation is for the restricted alternation-free fragment. §4: circuit transition is input-enabled and input-deterministic, with nonempty initial states. Associated Kripke structure adds a dummy initial state and shifts atoms by Next. Strong-fairness pair(a1,a2) requires a1 finitely often or a2 infinitely often. Validity is reduced to an initial formula output, no bad outputs and these fairness conditions; plain bounded safety search is not a complete substitute for fair reachability. §4 Proposition3 bounds latch count by |C|*k+|formula| for k path quantifiers; the paper defines circuit size as number of latches, abstracting the gate list. This does not bound every gate/transition-expression size by the same expression. Quantifier copies synchronize their starting latches; outputs track obligations and bad-state violations. Conjunction/Release circuit rules are explicitly omitted for space; correctness is sketched by structural induction. §5: implementation transforms AIGER circuits obtained by standard VHDL/Verilog synthesis; ABC supplies IC3/PDR, interpolation and BMC. Intel Core i5-4278U at2.6GHz. Defaults except starred Sym9; exact exceptional setting, timeout duration, RAM limit, repetitions and error bars are not specified. Dashes in BMC cells are not zero-second proofs, and TO is unresolved within an unspecified budget. §5.1: most I2C noninterference formulas intentionally fail because address/data transfer is the function of the bus. Failure alone is not a security vulnerability. NI3 holds with write enable off; NI5 fails because concurrent masters/arbitration affect later interpretation. Long-term NI7/8 fail, indicating information may persist. NI6 is listed/timed but has no separate prose explanation. §5.1: 3-bit address flow is determined for QNI1, while the log2(9)≈3.17-bit upper-bound query QNI2 times out. Neither quantitative-flow query is in Table1. The later assertion that all I2C properties were easily analyzed must be qualified by this reported timeout. §5.2: Bakery analysis is a synchronous finite Verilog model with select/pause inputs. Illegal select IDs advance process0. Excluding those paths, parameterizing tie resolution and contracting ID comparisons into one step change assumptions/model behavior before S3 is satisfied. Results do not show the unchanged original protocol is fully symmetric or prove starvation freedom/mutual exclusion under every scheduler. §5.2: printed S1–S3 use two universal path quantifiers, despite prose saying every execution has another swapped execution. Deterministic input-enabled circuit semantics support relating paired swapped inputs; do not silently rewrite the displayed formula to ∀∃. The weak-until rewrite removes a liveness-shaped part only under the stated input-determinism/input-enabledness conditions. §5.3: valid encoder properties depend on reset/control configuration and distinct data inputs. Huffman and8b10b are not error-correcting codes and only distance1 is expected. Hamming7–4 encodes4bits into7bits and is checked up to distance3. Active-high versus documented active-low reset is a specification/implementation discrepancy, not proof of failed correction on correctly configured messages. Printed source issues: §2 defines Release as ¬(¬phi1 U ¬phi1), repeating phi1 where standard duality uses phi2 on the right; visual PDF confirms. The §3.1 definition of K-equivalent languages is written only as an accepted-word implication, while later propositions use equivalence language. Record does not treat these presentation issues as an independent refutation of the algorithm. Hardware synthesis, circuit transformation, model semantics, specifications and ABC remain trusted. No proof certificates, independent checker or artifact execution are evaluated here. Claims of first/practical/industrial scale are author claims about selected cases. No Rust, Verus, TLA+ or LLM result is reported.
use_for_goal: Reader inference: directly useful for distributed mutual-exclusion specifications and evaluating LLM-written temporal properties that compare multiple executions. Trace relations express symmetry/noninterference beyond single-execution safety/liveness. Preserve synchronous timing, path quantifier order, temporal placement, reset/environment assumptions and finite process bounds. Counterexamples can expose scheduler defaults and ID-dependent delays before the critical section. The symbolic-circuit route does not itself supply a verified distributed implementation or unbounded-process proof.

title: An Alloy Verification Model for Consensus-Based Auction Protocols
what: Builds a machine-readable Alloy model of Max-Consensus Auction (MCA) protocols, separating bidding and agreement mechanisms from policy choices, and checks convergence to conflict-free allocations. title: Efficient Model Checking for the Alternating-Time µ-Calculus via Effectivity Frames
what: Implements full alternating-time µ-calculus (AMC) model checking over concurrent game frames (CGFs) and equivalent effectivity frames (EFs). title: An Elementary Formal Proof of the Group Law on Weierstrass Elliptic Curves in Any Characteristic
what: Lean 3/mathlib formalization of an abelian group on nonsingular points plus infinity of a full Weierstrass curve over any field, including characteristics two and three. Avoids a huge direct associativity expansion by mapping each point to an invertible ideal class, proving this map respects addition and is injective, then transferring group laws from the class group. Records singular-curve scope, explicit vertical/tangent/secant branches, nonsingular closure, coordinate-ring domain independent of discriminant, inverse/addition ideal identities, norm-degree obstruction and Smith-normal-form dimension argument. Preserves the unformalized geometric-model bridge and discriminant converse, representation/typeclass performance lessons, 1500-line algebraic proof comparison, experimental failed expansions and boundaries of cryptographic applicability.
assumptions_limits: §§2.1–2.3/3, pp.3–9: coefficients a1,a2,a3,a4,a6 define Y²+a1XY+a3Y=X³+a2X²+a4X+a6. General definitions start over a commutative ring, but group operations require a field for division. The point type is infinity or affine coordinates together with curve-membership and nonsingularity proof. The group theorem covers nonsingular points even when the curve discriminant is zero; an elliptic curve with invertible discriminant is a special case where all affine points qualify. Proposition 1/Remark 2/§4.4, pp.3–4/17: representing every abstract smooth projective genus-one curve equipped with an F-rational base point by a Weierstrass model is mathematical background via Riemann–Roch, not a formalized result of this development. Over rings the global-model claim requires restrictions such as trivial Picard group, and scheme-theoretic points differ from the affine-plus-infinity field representation. The paper does not prove the group theorem over arbitrary commutative rings. §2.2, p.5: affine nonsingularity means the equation holds and at least one partial derivative is nonzero. Nonzero discriminant implies every affine curve point is nonsingular by translating the point to the origin and using a coefficient calculation. The converse over the algebraic closure remains unformalized. Completing square/cube simplifies only when relevant characteristic is not two/three; the main full-model proof avoids those restrictions. §2.3, pp.6–8: infinity is identity; negation is (x,−y−a1x−a3). Equal x and opposite y gives infinity. Equal x but not opposite gives tangent slope −W_X/W_Y; unequal x gives secant slope (y1−y2)/(x1−x2). Cubic factorization gives x3=l²+a1l−a2−x1−x2, followed by reflected line value for y3. The slope function is total with zero in the vertical case; meaningful affine-sum lemmas require the guard excluding that case. Lemmas 5–6, pp.6–8: negation preserves nonsingularity directly. For nonvertical addition, differentiate the cubic factorization; if the third intersection x differs from the first two, a nonzero derivative proves nonsingularity, and otherwise the point equals an original point or its inverse. This establishes closure before relying on associativity. Addition on all affine points including singular ones would not yield a group. §3.1/Lemma 8, pp.9–10: coordinate ring F[W]=F[X,Y]/(W) is an integral domain by irreducibility of the monic quadratic in Y and degree comparison in X. This does not require discriminant nonzero. The ideal class group uses invertible fractional ideals modulo nonzero principal fractional ideals; it does not assume every nonzero ideal is invertible or prove the coordinate ring Dedekind. Lemma 10/§3.2, p.11: point ideal I(x,y)=(X−x,Y−y) is invertible for a nonsingular affine point because I(x,sigma_x(y)) I(x,y)=(X−x). Partial-derivative nonvanishing shows an auxiliary ideal is the unit ideal. Inverse fractional ideal is I(x,sigma_x(y))/(X−x). Infinity maps to the trivial class; additive type synonym adapts the multiplicative class group to the point-addition interface. Lemma 12/Remark 13, p.12: the nonvertical addition identity is I1 I2 (X−x3)=I3 (Y−lambda(X)). Principal factors vanish in the class group, so it proves preservation of addition. Tangent and secant are handled together under the nonvertical guard. The printed statement uses nonsingular points, but the underlying ideal identity does not require that; a more geometric three-intersection factorization would require stronger hypotheses. §3.3/Lemmas 14/16, pp.13–14: the coordinate ring has rank-two F[X] basis {1,Y}. Norm of p+qY is p²−pq(a1X+a3)−q²(X³+a2X²+a4X+a6), with degree max(2 deg p,2 deg q+3). The degree of the zero polynomial is treated as minus infinity in the degree formula. Even and odd leading degrees cannot cancel, and the mixed term has lower degree; no element has norm of degree one. Lemma 16–17, p.14: for nonzero f in this coordinate domain, Smith normal form equates degree of norm with F-dimension of the quotient by f. A point ideal quotient is F via evaluation, so if the point ideal were principal its generator would have norm degree one, contradiction. Trivial class therefore forces infinity; the already-established inverse/zero criterion reduces full injectivity to this kernel argument without assuming associativity of point addition. §3.3/Proposition 7, pp.9/14: injectivity and preservation of the explicit operation transfer associativity and commutativity from the existing class group. No surjectivity of to_class or identification of every ideal class with a rational point is needed. The final add_comm_group instance packages zero, inverse, addition and all laws. §4.1–4.2, pp.15–16: algebraic class-group argument spans about 1500 Lean 3 lines, reusing substantial algebra libraries. The cited Coq geometric comparison has 3500 divisor-theory plus 6500 curve-identification lines and different model/field scope. Direct general-position calculations reportedly involve tens of thousands of monomials and deterministic ring timeouts, while SageMath took about half a second. No hardware, systematic timings or controlled proof-strategy benchmark is given. §4.3, pp.16–17: nested univariate polynomials F[X][Y] make coefficient extraction and adjoin_root power basis convenient, but do not directly reuse multivariate Nullstellensatz lemmas. Explicit identities replace that machinery; partial derivatives are manually defined because coefficient differentiation is not a ring homomorphism accepted by polynomial.map. ring/linear_combination and a small eval_simp tactic discharge basic identities. §4.3, p.17: derived reducible comm_ring instance caused slow repeated unification despite an irreducible coordinate_ring type. Locally marking the instance irreducible fixes this Lean 3 issue; simplifying statement types fixes other timeouts. The publication predicts Lean 4 will address the issue, but this reading does not check current Lean/mathlib status. §4.4, p.17: base-change functoriality, division polynomials, reduction maps, cryptographic algorithms/protocols, Hasse bounds and abstract geometric equivalence are proposed or ongoing work. The record does not claim verified ECC machine code, constant-time implementation, cryptographic security, protocol correctness or independent build. Repository snapshot is supplied; actual source was not read here.
use_for_goal: Reader inference: useful proof-agent evaluation for replacing infeasible local algebra with an injective operation-preserving map into a known structure. Tests could cover theorem scope on singular curves, field/characteristic restrictions, total helpers with guards, dependency reuse and representation-induced timeouts. Offers a case where proof strategy and library interface matter more than brute-force tactic speed. Mathematical Lean work underlying potential cryptography, without a distributed protocol, Verus/Rust, TLA+ or LLM-agent experiment.

title: An End-To-End Verification of Keller’s Conjecture
what: Lean4 formalization resolving Keller cube-tiling conjecture in positive dimensions: true through7 and false from8 onward. Closes earlier gaps between a verified geometric-to-clique reduction and external SAT solving by verifying an improved coloring/CNF encoding, semantic symmetry transformations, certificate-checked propositional symmetry breaking and cube coverage, plus reflected checking of an8-dimensional counterexample and upward extension. Replaces arithmetic-heavy graph vertices by Keller colorings with Gap/No-Faceshare predicates; this enables the general s=2^(n−1) reduction to be solved directly at n7,s64, avoiding difficult unformalized discretization reductions to s3/4/6. Splits symmetry obligations at the conditional index-bit-flip boundary: this transformation is proved semantically in Lean, remaining clauses are manually designed and mechanically checked with substitution redundancy. Uses trestle’s scoped auxiliary variables and verified encoding combinators; optimized case splitting and checked cube-cover refutation complete the automated proof chain.
assumptions_limits: Tiling means axis-aligned translates of half-open unit cubes with exactly one covering cube for every point of R^n. Faceshare means corners differ by1 on one axis and agree on all others. This does not cover rotated cubes, overlaps, gaps or other tile shapes. The positive-dimension restriction matters: the displayed reduction theorem uses dimension n+1. The geometric reduction uses periodic tilings, finite clique/coloring existence with s=2^(n−1), and proof of encoding soundness in the direction needed to infer absence of colorings from UNSAT. Verifying only the SAT certificate would not suffice without those upstream connections. The authors avoid relying on Kisielewicz/Łysakowska discretization results, which Clune had not formalized, by solving s64 directly. Rows with s2 or s6 are additional experiments, not substitutes for the full n7 proof. Initial fixed-color symmetries for n≥3 assume the conjecture in dimension n−1. The authors prove n2 directly and proceed successively, rather than assuming the desired lower-dimensional cases. A unit-clause symmetry restriction is valid by existence of a transformed solution, not because every original solution satisfies it. Coordinate/color permutations and bit flips preserve the coloring conditions. Conditional index bit flips may change index adjacency yet preserve No-Faceshare. They are not expressible in the employed SR proof system; that portion requires separate Lean reasoning. The remaining SR clauses were found manually, not discovered automatically by a verified symmetry search. SR addition preserves satisfiability through a repair substitution and checked unit propagation, rather than necessarily preserving every satisfying assignment. Unverified C dsr-trim adds hints; verified trestle LSR checking validates its output. Failed or wrong hint generation should not be accepted merely because the converter terminates. The stated single-threaded CaDiCaL solving and proofix split suggestions are heuristic/unverified producers; solver results have certificates checked by verified LRAT/SR tools, and the cube-cover condition is separately refuted with negated cubes. The paper reports proof by reflection into Lean; it does not give a complete axiom/native-evaluation/trusted-executable inventory in this proceedings description. CNF auxiliaries yi,j,d and zi,j,d impose the implications needed for encoding, not an unconditional biconditional identification in every model. Exactly-one color constraints are essential for deriving color inequality from the no-shared-color clauses. Reported solve/check totals are hours over all cubes; they are not specified as elapsed wall time or normalized by a stated hardware/thread configuration. No CPU, RAM, repetitions or variance is supplied. Qualitative comparisons to BHMN are not a controlled ablation isolating encoding, splits and tooling. Authors explicitly report no LLM/AI use for the formalization; paper-writing use was limited to occasional Tikz-style questions. Thus this is evidence for human-designed hybrid formal proof workflows, not a measured LLM proof-agent success.
use_for_goal: Reader inference: strong example for evaluating agents that generate SAT encodings or formal specifications: a checked backend certificate does not validate a wrong source encoding, omitted symmetry cases or uncovered partitions. The compositional proof chain, untrusted hint/solver production and verified checking are directly useful evaluation patterns for distributed-system and Verus/TLA+ workflows. The subject itself is cube tiling; it contains no distributed protocol or Rust implementation and no LLM-agent experiment.

title: Program Analysis Is Harder Than Verification: A Computability Perspective
kind: computability theory of static analysis and verification
what: Defines a computability model of assertion domains, total recursive analyzers and total recursive verifiers, then studies when finding an assertion is reducible to checking one. An analyzer can always be converted constructively to an equally powerful verifier; the paper states a converse reduction for finite domains of assertions and an impossibility result for infinite domains under its stated conditions. An abstract domain is countable with a concretization into program sets and a decidable semantic implication relation; the base definition does not require a complete lattice. Verifiers return true or unknown, analyzers return an assertion, and soundness/completeness are defined independently. Extensional domains depend only on input-output semantics. Rice-style theorems 5.3/5.4 limit precise analyzers and nontrivial monotone precise verifiers to trivial extensional domains. Theorem 7.1 constructs a verifier by testing whether the analyzer result entails the requested assertion. Reasonable verifiers are nontrivial, monotone and finitely meet-closed. Theorem 7.6 constructs an equivalent analyzer on a nonempty finite domain by finite enumeration and a strongest verified assertion. Lemma 7.7 uses a countably infinite bounded-convergence domain whose equivalent analyzer would decide termination; Theorem 7.8 states the general impossibility of a total recursive verifier-to-equivalent-analyzer transformation for infinite domains. Examples distinguish semantic assertions from intensional resource assertions and connect the abstract framework to intervals and polyhedra.
numbers: Theorems 5.3/5.4: Rice-style limitations on precise procedures over extensional domains
Theorem 7.1: analyzer-to-equivalent-verifier transformation on any domain
Theorem 7.6: converse for nonempty finite domains and reasonable verifiers
Lemma 7.7/Theorem 7.8: infinite-domain impossibility via termination reduction
No empirical benchmark; results are computability theorems
Finite domains: analysis and verification equivalent (under stated reasonableness conditions)
Infinite domains: no constructive reduction from reasonable verifiers to equivalent analysers
assumptions_limits: The model uses deterministic Turing-complete programs and total recursive procedures; verifier unknown is allowed and is distinct from refutation. The finite converse requires the paper’s reasonable-verifier conditions, including finite meet closure. The infinite result concerns a general constructive reduction preserving assertion-proving power, not the claim that every concrete synthesis instance or infinite-domain analysis is uncomputable. These are computability statements, not practical running-time, NP-hardness or model-quality bounds. The theorem proofs are mathematical within the presented model; no mechanized proof artifact or empirical evaluation is reported.
use_for_goal: Supports separating proof or invariant generation from a trusted checking stage in Verus/TLA+/agent workflows. It explains why a checkable generated invariant does not imply a general procedure for discovering equally strong invariants. It does not establish any empirical advantage for LLM generation or a complexity bound for Rust/distributed-system proofs.
